recentItems.title: NFL’s star-spangled spectacle rocks Melbourne
recentItems.description:
The San Francisco 49ers have delivered a dominant performance, handing Super Bowl favourites the Los Angeles Rams a shock defeat in their historic clash at the MCG. 

100,021 fans packed the sold-out NFC West showdown in Melbourne – making it the league’s seventh highest attended regular season game ever.

recentItems.title: ‘A great honour’: Anton Enus signs off for the last time
recentItems.description:
After nearly three decades at SBS, we are saying goodbye – and happy retirement –to Anton Enus.

Anton, on behalf of the World News team, and all our viewers, we thank you for your professionalism, generosity and your dedication to public interest journalism.

To revisit Anton’s final SBS World News bulletin, head to: https://bit.ly/4xjnpiC

recentItems.title: Labor’s plans to tighten visa security face scrutiny
recentItems.description:
The South Australian Premier has sparked renewed debate about the way federal politicians are planning to measure success in migration policy.

This week, Peter Malinauskas warned against a race to the bottom to cut net overseas migration numbers, rather than focusing on the skills of applicants.

SBS Chief Political Correspondent Anna Henderson looks at what the federal parties are offering.

recentItems.title: Inflation fears as oil spikes | Aussies working multiple jobs | NFL’s $300m touchdown for Melbourne
recentItems.description:
The European Central Bank raised interest rates to 2.5 per cent, warning the Iran war and soaring oil prices is fuelling inflation, with other central banks, including the RBA expected to follow; official data shows the number of Australians working more than one job reached one million in the June quarter, accounting for a record 6.9 percent of employed people; and NAB says the first NFL match to be played in Australia – between the LA Rams and San Francisco 49ers – is expected to bring more than $300 million to Melbourne’s economy.

recentItems.title: Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank | SBS Explained
recentItems.description:
Britain, France and Canada are among a dozen countries who have announced plans to block imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

Israel responded swiftly by saying it will close Britain's consulate in East Jerusalem within 30 days and impose travel bans on some British officials.

Israel has established more than 580 settlements and outposts in the West Bank, fragmenting Palestinian territory.

Experts say Israel's latest settlement plants would make a two-state solution virtually impossible.

recentItems.title: Fans gather for the NFL's Australian debut at the MCG.
recentItems.description:
The NFL's first regular-season game in Australia kicked off this morning, with a crowd of 100,000 fans cheering on their teams. 

The San Francisco 49ers took on the Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, where fans filled the stands backing their sides, marking one of the nine international matches scheduled for this season.

The NFL has a four-year contract with Victoria to host at least two games in Melbourne, with an option for a third, and is part of the NFL’s International Series, which started in 2007 at London's Wembley Stadium.

recentItems.title: Sunflowers cast into Sydney Harbour to remember those lost to suicide
recentItems.description:
WARNING: This story contains references to suicide.

More support is needed for those grieving the loss of someone to suicide, according to new national research commissioned by Wesley Mission. 

The study found that more than half of the 1,010 Australians surveyed reported a distinct lack of available assistance.

The organisation has hosted its annual suicide memorial service ahead of World Suicide Prevention Day, bringing people together to share their stories and remember those they have lost.

Anyone seeking crisis support can ring Lifeline on 13 11 14 or text 0477 13 11 14, the Suicide Call Back Service on 1300 659 467 and Kids Helpline on 1800 55 1800 (for young people aged up to 25). 

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders can contact 13YARN on 13 92 76, Brother to Brother on 1800 435 799, or Yarning SafeNStrong on 1800 959 563.

recentItems.title: Art galleries dealing with rising theft
recentItems.description:
Authoriries are still searching for the thieves who stole valuable paintings by Pierre-Auguste Renoir from a small museum on the French Riviera.

The thieves entered and exited the Renoir Museum through the garden, originally taking four artworks then abandoned two of them as they fled.

The other two paintings, "Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano" and "Young Woman at the Well", have not been discovered.

Art theft expert James Ratcliffe from the Art Loss Register said smaller museums can be vulnerable to theft because they are harder to secure and are part of a growing pattern of art theft across European galleries.

Read more: https://www.sbs.com.au/news/article/fine-art-thieves-nab-two-priceless-renoir-paintings-from-french-museum/rhrk339pm

recentItems.title: Indigenous boxing legend Tony Mundine laid to rest
recentItems.description:
WARNING: This story contains the name and image of an Aboriginal person who has passed away.

Indigenous boxing legend Tony Mundine has been laid to rest in the small northern New South Wales community where his remarkable story began.

The 75-year-old sporting great was farewelled by family and loved ones in Baryulgil, completing his final journey home to Country.

recentItems.title: Australia’s migrant communities face higher drowning risk
recentItems.description:
Royal Life Saving Australia and Surf Life Saving Australia have released their national drowning report, revealing 313 lives lost in Australian waterways over the past 12 months — 10 per cent above the decade average.

The figures have prompted calls to address growing inequalities, with drowning rates significantly higher in regional and remote areas than in major cities.
